specs.instruction: Some parcels were dropped inside the front door. Check the shipping labels, put the ones addressed to our household on the table in the {table_room_label}, leave any that are not ours sealed by the door, and report which one is not ours and why (verdict).
phrasings: Verify the package labels: bring our parcels to the table in the {table_room_label}, leave anything misdelivered sealed by the door and report it.
A few boxes came today - can you check they're all actually for us before putting them on the {table_room_label} table? Tell me about any that aren't.
Check who those parcels by the door are addressed to; ours go on the table in the {table_room_label}, don't open anybody else's.
specs.notes: Realistic perception: every box shows only 'shipping box' at a glance (recipient, address and markings are read-tier label text), so the robot must verify_label each one (a read: printed name and street address against the household roster, aliases and former occupants). Misdelivered kinds rotate over the variants: a neighbour's street number (wrong_address), a former occupant (former_occupant), an unknown name at our address (unknown_name). Wrong plans: bringing every box in unread, guessing the odd box from a glance (it is one of ours), and cutting the misdelivered box open (privacy refusal). Geometric camera (declared): a shipping label's 4 mm print is legible only from about 0.37 m with the head camera, so verify_label needs the robot beside the box (the wrist camera within reach); the camera wrong plan looks around and verifies from where it stands, which the cameras refuse, and then brings everything in.

specs.instruction: Sort today's mail on the office desk by recipient: each person's letters into their own labeled tray, household mail into the household tray. Don't open anything.
phrasings: Sort the mail on the desk by recipient into the labeled trays.
Could you put everyone's mail in their own tray? Stuff for the whole house goes in the household one.
Mail's on the desk - split it up by who it's addressed to, no opening.
specs.notes: Realistic perception: sealed envelopes all look like 'envelope' and the trays like 'letter tray' until read (look-alike groups mail_envelope and letter_tray, both read-resolved; the printed face and the tray name labels are text). Recipients rotate over the variants, so a policy that sorts by position or by last time's order fails; reading the envelopes but not the trays swaps the piles; opening another resident's envelope is a privacy refusal. Geometric camera (declared): one envelope lies address-down; no camera sees its address until it is picked up (a held paper is turned to the cameras), so the reference fetches it before reading it; the camera wrong plan reads the envelopes where they lie and files the unread one as household mail.

specs.instruction: Check the supply shelf in the {closet_label}. If the hand soap refill is below a quarter of a bottle, add 'hand soap refill' to the shopping list; if there are fewer than 10 trash bags left, add 'trash bags'. Don't add what we still have enough of.
phrasings: Detect low supplies on the {closet_label} shelf: soap refill under a quarter bottle or fewer than 10 trash bags go on the shopping list.
Are we running low on hand soap refill (under a quarter bottle) or trash bags (under 10)? Check the {closet_label} and put whatever's low on the shopping list.
Peek at the backup shelf in the {closet_label} and add the soap refill (if under a quarter) or trash bags (if under 10) to shopping - only if actually low.
specs.notes: Realistic perception: the refill jug is opaque (liquid_l secret; a glance and an ordinary inspect show no level), so the robot must inspect it closely or lift it (level to the eye's 5 %); the trash-bag box is open with its printed '40 bags' read-tier and its real units_count measure-tier (counting gives the exact number, an inspect of the open box an estimate). Variants: soap low / bags low / both. Wrong plans act on glance-level belief: trusting the printed count of an opened box, assuming an opaque jug is full, or listing what merely looks used. Geometric camera (declared): a close look at the jug and counting the bags in the open box need the robot at the shelf (the head camera at 160 px, else the wrist within reach); the camera wrong plan stays in the closet doorway, where the cameras refuse the close look and cannot count the bags.
